question.problem:
A company is selling a new product on three e-commerce platforms, platform $1,$ platform $2,$ and platform $3.$

- $44%$ of customers bought the product on platform $1,$ and $70%$ of those customers were satisfied with the product.

- $25%$ of customers bought the product on platform $2,$ and $85%$ of those customers were satisfied with the product.

- $31%$ of customers bought the product on platform $3.$

If $25%$ of all customers are teenagers, $60%$ of teenage customers are satisfied with the product, and $20%$ of satisfied customers are teenagers, what is the probability that a randomly chosen customer from platform $3$ is satisfied? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let $T$ be the event that a customer is a teenager, $S$ be the event that a customer is satisfied, and ${P}_{1},{P}_{2},{P}_{3}$ be the event that a customer bought the product on platform $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively. 

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

- From the bullet points, we have the following information:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P({P}_{1})=0.44 &  & P(S|{P}_{1})=0.7 \\  & P({P}_{2})=0.25 &  & P(S|{P}_{2})=0.85 \\  & P({P}_{3})=0.31\end{aligned}
$$

The disjoint union ${P}_{1}⊔{P}_{2}⊔{P}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space, and we have

$$
P({P}_{1})+P({P}_{2})+P({P}_{3})=0.44+0.25+0.31=1.
$$

- Since $25%$ of all customers are teenagers, we have

$$
P(T)=0.25.
$$

- Since $60%$ of teenage customers are satisfied, we have

$$
P(S|T)=0.6.
$$

- Since $20%$ of satisfied customers are teenagers, we have

$$
P(T|S)=0.2.
$$

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen customer from platform $3$ is satisfied with the product, which is represented as $P(S|{P}_{3}).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(T|S) & =\frac{P(S|T)P(T)}{P(S)} \\ 0.2 & =\frac{P(S|T)P(T)}{P(S|{P}_{1})P({P}_{1})+P(S|{P}_{2})P({P}_{2})+P(S|{P}_{3})P({P}_{3})} \\ 0.2 & =\frac{(0.60)(0.25)}{(0.7)(0.44)+(0.85)(0.25)+P(S|{P}_{3})(0.31)} \\ 0.2 & =\frac{0.15}{0.5205+0.31P(S|{P}_{3})}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation for $P(S|{P}_{3}),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.2(0.5205+0.31P(S|{P}_{3})) & =0.15 \\ 0.5205+0.31P(S|{P}_{3}) & =\frac{0.15}{0.2} \\ 0.5205+0.31P(S|{P}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4} \\ 0.31P(S|{P}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4}-0.5205 \\ P(S|{P}_{3}) & =\frac{1}{0.31}(\frac{3}{4}-0.5205) \\ P(S|{P}_{3}) & ≈0.740\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
